It is made from a country holding a line it can hold, with ten departments still under occupation, which is the whole difficulty: any terms available now leave some of France where it currently is. That is why this was never seriously attempted. No French government of 1917 could have signed terms leaving the occupied departments in German hands and survived the signing. What actually happened: No French government approached Germany in 1917. The spring brought the Sixtus affair, a private approach by the Austrian Emperor through his brother-in-law, Prince Sixtus of Bourbon-Parma, which came to nothing and was exposed in April 1918. Painleve's brief ministry in the autumn of 1917 gave way to Clemenceau's on 16 November, which was formed to make war to the end and did. A negotiated peace in 1917 would have left Germany in occupation of northern France and most of Belgium, and no French cabinet could have signed it and remained in office. The idea that peace might have been had in that year survived in French politics as an accusation for years.▶ A NOTE FOR THE
